sql_threads.py:133-157,175-195 use Future() standalone. In CPython's concurrent.futures._base.Future, cancel() returns False in RUNNING/FINISHED states and True in PENDING (and for already-cancelled futures). set_running_or_notify_cancel moves PENDING to RUNNING (returns True) or returns False for a cancelled future. set_result/set_exception, done, cancelled, exception and add_done_callback do not need an executor. The worker guards set_exception with done(), which avoids InvalidStateError. _log_call_after_cancel checks cancelled() before exception(), so it does not raise CancelledError. Based on my knowledge of the stdlib state machine; I did not read the stdlib source in this environment.

sql_threads.py:184-195. asyncio.wait does not cancel the awaited future on timeout, so the concurrent future stays cancellable. In CPython, wrap_future calls _chain_future, which registers a done-callback on the source concurrent future. That callback runs _copy_future_state, which calls dest.cancel() when source.cancelled(), via call_soon_threadsafe. So a successful future.cancel() resolves the wrapper as cancelled and it does not hang. Here the wrapper is not awaited after a successful cancel (SqlWorkersBusyError is raised), and a cancelled future raises no 'never retrieved' warning. If cancel() fails because the call is running, `await result` waits for the real result. This is from my knowledge of the CPython stdlib; I did not read the stdlib source in this environment.

sql_threads.py:112-115 creates workers with daemon=True. In CPython 3.9+, threading._shutdown joins only non-daemon threads, so daemon workers never delay exit. concurrent.futures.thread registers _python_exit via threading._register_atexit, which sets the global shutdown flag and joins every worker in _threads_queues, regardless of shutdown(wait=False). Since 3.9 its workers are non-daemon. A stuck driver call would therefore block exit. Counter-input considered: a daemon worker blocked in a driver call at shutdown. It does not hold up exit; the interpreter finalizes without joining it. The docstring is accurate. This rests on my knowledge of CPython; I did not run it.

The prior defect is fixed at head. In sql_threads.py:145-153 the outer `except BaseException` logs and then, if `not future.done()`, calls `future.set_exception(exc)`, so the awaiting `asyncio.wrap_future(future)` in run_blocking_sql (line 184, 191) completes with the exception. A failure of set_running_or_notify_cancel leaves the future PENDING, and set_exception works on it. A failure of set_result or set_exception leaves it not done, so the fallback completes it. A cancelled future is already done and its caller has already been woken. Only a second failure inside the fallback itself is merely logged (line 153), and that is a double fault outside the claim's scope.
